prompt.context: Our client is a private equity firm which has invested in FoodCo, a family-owned $19M branded frozen ethnic foods manufacturer operating out of the Northeast.
prompt.question: How can FoodCo triple their profitability over the next 2 years?

clarifying_info.q: What is the current profit level?
clarifying_info.a: Profit is currently $3M, so the target is $9M.
No. We are extremely capital constrained and cannot look to increase production by opening a new plant.
For the purposes of this case, assume the sole revenue-generating stream is ethnic food sold in cups (e.g. a cup of noodles).
No. Benchmarking has determined that the ideal price is already being charged to customers.

clarifying_info.q: Are there major market changes to consider?
clarifying_info.a: Assume there are no major changes in the market.

exhibits.title: Labor Efficiency Breakdown
exhibits.shows: A chart breaking down how labor time is currently allocated, highlighting repair time as a major component relative to benchmark.
exhibits.data: Current repair time is approximately 22% of labor time; benchmark/industry figure is referenced for comparison.

framework: Market: assess competitive environment and demand (assume no major changes for this case)

Revenues: evaluate price (fixed by benchmarking), revenue streams (cups only, capital-constrained on volume), and quantity growth options (national retail/food service expansion, new products/channels organically or via acquisition)
Costs: identify and prioritize cost categories — Labor (50%), Equipment (25%), Administrative (20%), Other (5%); focus on Labor as the largest and most controllable driver
Efficiency: analyze labor time breakdown (productive time vs. repair/downtime) and quantify savings from reducing repair time
Investment decision: weigh cost of efficiency investment against profit improvement to validate ROI

questions.prompt: Given the cost breakdown — Labor 50%, Equipment 25%, Administrative 20%, Other 5% — which area would you target and why?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify Labor (50%) as the primary target because it is the largest cost driver and more controllable than equipment or administrative costs. Strong answers note that for a manufacturing business this ratio is unusually high, signaling operational inefficiency.

questions.prompt: The exhibit shows that repair time currently accounts for 22% of labor time. Through training and reconfiguration of equipment we can reduce repair time to 5% with a $500,000 investment. Should we make this investment?
questions.guidance: Candidate must calculate total labor cost, quantify the savings from reducing repair time, compare to the investment, and conclude yes/no with a clear rationale. Strong answers walk through each step explicitly and state a clear recommendation.

math.setup: Total costs = Revenues - Profit = $19M - $3M = $16M. Labor cost = $16M * 50% = $8M. Repair time reduction = 22% - 5% = 17%. Annual savings = 17% * $8M = $1.36M. Payback = $500K / $1.36M < 1 year.
math.answer: Yes, we should invest. Annual savings of $1.36M more than recover the $500K investment within the first year.

questions.prompt: (Bonus) Efficiency savings also translate into higher production volumes. Assuming the 17% efficiency gain translates directly to a 17% increase in production volume, what is the new revenue figure?
questions.guidance: Candidate should apply the efficiency percentage as a volume multiplier to current revenues. Strong answers note that this is an approximation and that actual revenue uplift depends on demand absorption and pricing remaining constant.

math.answer: New revenue = $22.23M, implying revenue growth of approximately $3.23M.

brainstorming.prompt: What ideas do you have to improve operational efficiency and reduce costs?

categories.name: Labor
ideas: Reduce machine repair/downtime through technician training
Reconfigure equipment layout to minimize idle time
Cross-train workers to cover multiple functions

categories.name: Equipment
ideas: Upgrade aging equipment to reduce failure rate
Negotiate better service contracts to lower repair costs
Invest in automation for repetitive tasks

categories.name: Revenue Growth (longer-term)
ideas: Launch new ethnic food products (new SKUs)

recommendation: Invest the $500K to reduce repair time from 22% to 5% through training and equipment reconfiguration; this generates $1.36M in annual cost savings and a 17% volume increase, lifting revenue to ~$22.23M
Combined effect raises profitability to approximately $3M + $1.36M (cost savings) + margin on incremental $3.23M revenue, totaling roughly $7M — short of the $9M target
risks: Efficiency gains may not fully translate to revenue if demand cannot absorb the extra 17% volume
Capital constraints limit ability to pursue complementary growth levers simultaneously
Family-owned culture may create resistance to operational changes and headcount adjustments
next_steps: Execute the $500K training and equipment reconfiguration program immediately
Quantify demand upside to validate whether the volume increase is absorbable at current price
Identify additional cost reduction levers (equipment, administrative) to close the remaining ~$2M gap to the $9M profit target
Evaluate national retail and food service expansion as longer-horizon revenue plays
